texts: (Astronomer's Note: Discovered by Jocelyn Bell just 5 years ago. Very very recent by astronomical standards)
(Astronomer's Note: Hundreds of rotations per second. Very very fast by anyone's standards)

Neutron Star - A recently discovered celestial body that is the collapsed core of a massive star, condensed to a small body.











Neutron Stars no longer undergo fusion, but still release latent HEAT AND LIGHT, much like a white dwarf star.

Neutron Stars potentially consist of mostly neutrons, as the immense pressure combines protons and electrons into neutrons. 

Neutron Stars rotate at high speeds, conserving their angular momentum at a smaller volume.
(Astronomer's Note: ~10km in diameter. Very very small by astronomical standards)
(Astronomer's Note: Astronomers refer to all elements heavier than Hydrogen and Helium as metals. Eat it, chemists.)

Star - a massive sphere of plasma held together by its own gravity, which radiates light and heat from nuclear fusion in its core. 






Stars fuse atoms to create almost all elements larger than Lithium (atomic number 3). 


Metallicity - The proportion of metallic elements to nonmetallic elements. Younger stars will have a higher metallicity, since they are formed from the fused remnants of older stars.

White Dwarf Star - A stellar remnant that no longer conducts nuclear fusion. 






The vast majority of stars eventually become white dwarf stars because they do not have enough mass to condense into a neutron star or blackhole.
(Astronomer's Note: They still are bright and hot from residual heat)
